goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without checking the `embeddable_host` key exists, raising NoMethodError on nil when the key is missing

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` without first ensuring `params[:embeddable_host]` is present. If a request is sent without the `embeddable_host` key (malformed client, manual request, etc.), `params[:embeddable_host]` will be `nil` and `[:host]` will raise `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500 instead of a controlled 4xx error. There is no guarding logic in the diff to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The host validation regex permits an optional port but `record_for_host` matches against `uri.host` which excludes the port, so a host saved as `example.com:8080` will never match any referer and is permanently unusable

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex allows a port suffix (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and the `before_validation` normalizer strips scheme and path but does **not** strip the port, so a saved value like `example.com:8080` is possible. However `record_for_host` parses the referer/embed URL via `URI(host)` and compares against `uri.host` (hostname only, excludes port) with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That means a record stored with a port will never match any incoming URL (even `http://example.com:8080/...`), making it unusable for `host_allowed?` checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In `_hydrateEmbedded`, the plural branch's `obj[k].map(...)` always returns a truthy array making `|| []` dead code, can produce literal `false` entries when `_lookupSubType` returns false, and deletes `obj[k]` unconditionally even when hydration failed

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural-handling branch does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` and then `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []; delete obj[k];`. Since `Array#map` always returns an array (truthy even when empty), `|| []` is effectively dead code. More importantly, unlike the singular branch (which only `delete obj[k]` when hydration succeeds), the plural branch always deletes the original `*_ids` and assigns the mapped results even if `_lookupSubType` returns falsy values for some/all IDs, potentially leaving `false`/`undefined` entries and losing the original IDs. This is a concrete correctness regression introduced by the diff.

The TLD portion of the host validation regex is limited to `{2,5}` characters, rejecting valid domains with longer TLDs like `.museum` or `.technology`

adjudication.rationale: In the new model `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, `validates_format_of :host` uses the regex `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`, which restricts the TLD to 2–5 letters (`[a-z]{2,5}`). This will reject valid longer TLDs such as `.museum` or `.technology`, so the finding points to a real correctness limitation introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `category_id` is persisted without verifying the category exists and the `belongs_to :category` association has no presence/foreign-key validation, so a bogus id saves fine but later breaks topic embedding and frontend badge display

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, `host.category_id` is assigned directly from params (or set to `uncategorized_category_id` only if blank), with no check that the referenced category exists. The `EmbeddableHost` model has `belongs_to :category` but no presence/existence validation, and the migration creates `category_id` as `null: false` without any foreign key constraint. So an invalid/nonexistent `category_id` can be persisted. That can later cause failures or incorrect behavior when code relies on the association/id (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import` passes `eh.try(:category_id)` into `PostCreator`, and the admin UI renders `host.category` for `category-badge`, which may be nil/unresolvable if the id is bogus).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `update` action in EmbeddingController ignores params entirely and just re-renders current state, making the PUT endpoint a no-op API that appears to save but persists nothing

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action does not read or apply any `params` or persist anything; it just re-renders the same `@embedding` built by `fetch_embedding` (an `OpenStruct` with `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`). The corresponding client controller action `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would hit this PUT endpoint, but the server-side PUT is effectively a no-op and cannot save any changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The spec files for embeddable_hosts_controller and embedding_controller only assert the controller's superclass and contain no request-level tests for the CRUD endpoints, leaving them effectively untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new controller specs: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb. Each contains only a single example asserting the controller inherits from Admin::AdminController, and neither issues any requests (e.g., GET/PUT/POST/DELETE) to exercise the newly added endpoints in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController (create/update/destroy) or Admin::EmbeddingController (show/update). So the CRUD behavior introduced by the diff is effectively not covered by request-level/controller tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The migration uses `force: true` to silently drop any pre-existing table and unconditionally deletes old site settings rows in a non-reversible `change` block, risking loss of original configuration on a failed partial run

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` does `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which will drop/recreate the table if it already exists (data-loss risk if the table is present for any reason when the migration runs). It also uses a `change` method with raw `execute` statements that insert and then `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`, making the migration effectively irreversible (no `down`/`reversible` block) and permanently removing prior configuration values.
